explanation: Methane, CH4, has one carbon and four hydrogen atoms, while carbon dioxide, CO2, has three atoms. Yet carbon dioxide is the heavier molecule, at about 44 atomic mass units to methane's 16.

claims.text: A methane molecule, CH4, has five atoms: one carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms.
A carbon dioxide molecule, CO2, has three atoms: one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms.
The molecular mass of carbon dioxide is about 44 atomic mass units and that of methane about 16.
